_comment: First draft for the top Hong Kong apps: each runs to its first content or its login gate. Texts are unverified until a board run passes them. Spotify and Uber wait longer: 60 s after launch the board still showed their splash screens. WhatsApp shows its companion-device screen (a QR code to link it to a phone) where the device has no telephony, as the board doesn't: either gate passes. Uber's login screen says "You consent to receive a verification code": no consent step there, its Continue button would submit an empty number. Viber's start is its own button. Instagram's terms screen comes after its splash: it is waited for before the consent step. Uber's sign-in is a web page in its EmbeddedWebView, whose text neither the view dump nor the node dump carries: its check is that the native welcome or the web sign-in is on screen. Instagram's onboarding after its terms reads Join Instagram / Get started / I already have a profile.

com.instagram.android.text: ^(Log in|Create new account|Get started|I already have a profile)$
